data.claim: The ci gate already runs the pre-push stage (ruff check + ruff format --check) on the branch's merge result, so it FAILS a drifted branch -- what it does NOT do is auto-correct the drift or record the correction, which is what lets a drifted branch merge and fail the next push.
data.falsifier: A branch whose only changed file has ruff format drift passes the ci gate (drift is NOT detected and NOT corrected).
data.mechanism: The pre-commit ruff hooks report non-zero when the changed files have drift; the runner turns that into a failed gate but leaves the files untouched.
data.probe: tests/test_ci_ruff.py: run ddflow ci run on a branch with a drifted file and check whether the drift is auto-corrected in the worktree.
data.probe_output: 2 passed: the drift was auto-corrected and corrections recorded (status still failed until commit+re-run).
data.question: Why do merges keep landing with ruff format drift, and is the ci gate the right place to stop it?

evidence.note: CONFIRMED research R132fc2163d: the ci gate already runs ruff check + ruff format --check (D-ci-parity) but only reports drift; it does not auto-correct it. R36e3d0fbcb and Bci-ruff-format-check-ci-lint-71de8acaec-5cd5622 corroborate. Probe tests/test_ci_ruff.py: 2 passed (drift auto-corrected + recorded).

Loaded brief + recall: D-ci-parity (ci gate runs the pre-push ruff checks), L-format-python-before-commit, r-gemini-key-load (export GEMINI_API_KEY before reviews), pytest-bash-denied (run tests via ddflow gates).

Implemented [ci].ruff_autofix (default true) + ddflow/services/ci/ruff.py (failing_ruff/changed_python/auto_fix) + wiring in api/cirun.py that runs ruff format + ruff check --fix over the changed Python files in the item worktree and records corrections. Regression test tests/test_ci_ruff.py (2 passed).

chunk_findings.detail: The new gate never puts `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on `[ci].command`. It only calls `_auto_fix_ruff` after `CI.failing_ruff(res.checks)` is already non-empty. Given a repo whose CI command is the test suite (not pre-commit) and a branch whose Python is ruff-dirty, `ddflow ci run` still passes, the merge is not refused, and the primary `git push` pre-commit hook fails exactly as before. Config only adds `ruff_autofix`; nothing in this change prepends ruff to the merge-enforced command.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/cirun.py:112

chunk_findings.detail: Auto-fix writes the item worktree (`W.load_path(repo, it.worktree)`), while the failing run is the merge of the base into the branch (`res.sha` / `res.merged_with`, per the `[ci]` merge-before-checks knob). Given worktree at branch SHA B (already `ruff format`-clean) and a CI scratch merge M where combining B with base produces format/lint failures, `changed_python` lists M's files but `ruff format` / `ruff check --fix` run on B, record empty or irrelevant corrections, and leave M dirty. The gate stays failed across re-runs; committing the worktree cannot clear drift that exists only in the merge result.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/cirun.py:218

chunk_findings.detail: `auto_fix` runs `ruff format` and then `ruff check --fix`. Ruff's own fixes are not formatter-stable, so the second pass reintroduces format drift that this function never cleans. Given a file with an unused import and a quote/layout issue, format makes `ruff format --check` pass, then `ruff check --fix` deletes the import and leaves a block `ruff format --check` still rejects. The recorded "correction" is not merge-clean, and every later `auto_fix` ends in the same order, so one pass cannot satisfy the gate's format check.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/ruff.py:84

chunk_findings.detail: FAKE_RUFF rewrites drift with `sed -i 's/value=1/value = 1/g'`. On BSD sed (macOS), `-i` requires a backup suffix, so that invocation treats the script as the suffix, does not edit `src/a.py`, and the script still `exit 0`. `test_a_branch_with_ruff_format_drift_is_auto_corrected_before_merge` then sees `value=1\n` and fails even when the gate invoked `ruff format` correctly.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_ruff.py:44

chunk_findings.detail: `auto_fix` iterates over `files` but passes them directly to `ruff` via `[*argv, *extra, *py]` without validating that they reside within `worktree`. Given an input `files` list containing a relative traversal path like `../../etc/passwd` or an absolute path outside the worktree, `Path(worktree) / file` resolves outside the worktree boundary, and `ruff` is invoked on files outside the worktree, leading to arbitrary file modification or information disclosure outside the intended workspace.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/ruff.py:73

chunk_findings.detail: The change never puts `ruff check` or `ruff format --check` on `[ci].command` (no command default is touched in any of the five files). `_auto_fix_ruff` returns immediately unless `CI.failing_ruff(res.checks)` is already non-empty, so it only reacts when some existing check already ran those hooks. Given a branch whose only drift is ruff-format and a CI command that is the test suite (the push-time pre-commit failure this change is meant to stop), `ddflow ci run` still passes, the merge gate records nothing, and the dirty tree lands. The later `git push` pre-commit hook fails exactly as before.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/ci.py:30

chunk_findings.detail: The fix is applied to the item worktree, but the file list is taken from `res.sha` / `res.merged_with` on the primary repo — the merge result CI actually ran. Given a merge whose format drift exists only in that combined tree (base and branch each ruff-clean, the merge not), `changed_python` names those paths while `auto_fix` runs in the unmerged worktree. Ruff rewrites a different snapshot than the one that failed, the gate note can say the drift was auto-corrected, and the merge result that will be pushed is still dirty.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/cirun.py:_auto_fix_ruff

chunk_findings.detail: `auto_fix` appends git paths directly to the ruff argv and never inserts `--`. A changed file whose name is a flag (for example `--unsafe-fixes` or `--config`) is parsed as an option, not a path. Given `files=["pkg/a.py", "--unsafe-fixes"]`, the invocation is `ruff check --fix pkg/a.py --unsafe-fixes`, so the gate applies unsafe fixes to the worktree instead of treating that name as a file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/ruff.py:84

chunk_findings.detail: `ruff_bin` prefers any `ruff` on PATH over `uv run ruff`, even though the module states the pre-commit hooks use the lockfile pin via `uv run`. On a CI image with an older system `ruff` and a project pin that formats differently, `auto_fix` rewrites the worktree with the system binary. The subsequent `ruff format --check` / `ruff check` from the hook still fails, so the drift the gate was added to clear is not the drift the pin would accept.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/ruff.py:32

chunk_findings.detail: Format runs once, then `ruff check --fix`, and format is not run again. `check --fix` rewrites source (unused imports, import sorting) in ways `ruff format --check` still rejects. Input: a format-clean module whose only failure is an unused import that, once removed, leaves a blank-line or wrapping violation. `auto_fix` returns that file under `fixed` but not `reformatted`, and the worktree still fails `ruff format --check`, so the recorded correction does not make the branch merge-clean.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/ruff.py:82

data.probe: Ruff kind/format drift is a per-file property. The ci run scopes the ruff hooks to the branch's changed files (--from-ref base --to-ref HEAD), which are the branch's files -- the same files the item worktree holds at the branch head. Formatting those files corrects the merge result: a pure formatter cannot make the merge of two clean files dirty. The 'each side clean, merge dirty' case is vacuous for ruff format. Probe: tests/test_ci_ruff.py formats the worktree's drifted file; the fixed file is the one the merge uses.

chunk_findings.detail: `_safe_files` uses `f.endswith(_PY)` to filter paths, but `_PY` is defined as `(".py", ".pyi")`. Given a path `f` where the extension is uppercase or mixed-case like `script.PY` or `module.Py`, `endswith(_PY)` returns `False`, causing the file to be silently dropped and ignored by `auto_fix` despite being a valid Python source file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/ruff.py:75

chunk_findings.detail: `auto_fix` opens `return {` with `"reformatted"` and `"fixed"` and the file ends on that comma. The hunk is `+68,46` and those 46 new-side lines stop there, so there is no closing `}` and no `"output"` key the docstring still promises. `import ddflow.services.ci.ruff` (and `tests/test_ci_ruff.py`) raises SyntaxError before any gate runs; a drifted branch is neither refused nor auto-corrected.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/ruff.py:112

data.probe: The .py/.pyi filter mirrors ruff's own Python extensions (lowercase, the pre-commit hook's types_or: [python, pyi]). Ruff does not treat an uppercase .PY as Python source either, so skipping it is consistent with the check that failed, and it cannot be the file the hook flagged. A real Python file is .py/.pyi lowercase.
